evals.prompt:
Create a component contract for a Badge component. Here are the answers to all interview questions:
1. Name: Badge
2. Purpose: A small pill-shaped label that displays a status, category, or count — appears attached to other components or inline in text.
3. Composition: Standalone — owns its content directly. No sub-components.
4. Zones: One zone — the label. It shows content (text or a number). Exactly 1 instance. Position is fixed (always centred within the badge). No interaction zone.
5. Variants: Three sizes (sm, md, lg) and four semantic styles (neutral, info, success, error).
6. Layout flexibility: None — layout is always the same.
7. Adaptive layout: No — layout is identical regardless of available space.
8. Interactions: Nothing — display only.
9. Platform: Web browser only.
10. Interaction delta: N/A — single platform.
11. States: None beyond default.
12. Token source: Description only — mark as pending.
13. Token naming: color- prefix (e.g., color-surface-neutral).
14. JSON schema: No.

Save the file to /tmp/Badge.md
evals.expected_output: A complete Badge.md with all 6 sections. Token map marked pending. Semantic markup uses a non-interactive element (span or similar). Size and style variants in §3.2. Accessibility notes the decorative/display-only nature.

evals.prompt:
Create a component contract for a Modal Dialog component. Here are the answers to all interview questions:
1. Name: Modal
2. Purpose: A centered overlay that presents focused content and blocks interaction with the rest of the page until dismissed.
3. Composition: Standalone shell — owns its zones directly. Contains: a header zone (title + optional close button), a scrollable body zone, and a footer zone (action buttons).
4. Zones:
   - Title zone: Content type, cardinality 1, fixed — top of header, accepts text string.
   - Close button zone: Interaction type (triggers dismiss action), cardinality 0–1, fixed — top-right corner.
   - Body zone: Content type, cardinality 1, flexible, accepts any content.
   - Footer zone: Content type, cardinality 0–1, flexible — bottom, accepts 1–3 action buttons.
5. Variants: Two sizes (default, large).
6. Layout flexibility: None.
7. Adaptive layout: No.
8. Interactions: Close button click dismisses the modal. Backdrop click optionally dismisses. Escape key dismisses.
9. Platform: Both web and mobile.
10. Interaction delta: No — same interactions on all platforms.
11. States: Loading (body content loading), disabled (actions disabled during async operation).
12. Token source: Coded reference. Use these CSS custom properties as if from the component stylesheet: --color-overlay-backdrop: rgba(0,0,0,0.5), --radius-modal: 8px, --spacing-modal-padding: 24px.
13. Token naming: --color-, --radius-, --spacing- (CSS custom properties).
14. JSON schema: Yes. Draft 07. Use $ref for sub-components.

Save both files to /tmp/
evals.expected_output: Modal.md with all 6 sections. Token map populated from the CSS vars with source noted. Accessibility must document focus trap (Yes), aria-modal, aria-labelledby, Escape key. Schema file Modal.schema.json with correct structure.

evals.prompt:
Create a component contract for a Notification Toast component. Here are the answers to all interview questions:
1. Name: Toast
2. Purpose: A transient notification that appears at the edge of the screen to inform the user of an event, then auto-dismisses.
3. Composition: Composite shell wrapping: an Icon sub-component (has its own contract), a text content area (title + optional body), and an optional close Button sub-component (has its own contract).
4. Zones:
   - Icon zone: Content type, cardinality 0–1, fixed — left of text content. Accepts Icon component only.
   - Title zone: Content type, cardinality 1, fixed — above body text. Accepts text string.
   - Body zone: Content type, cardinality 0–1, flexible. Accepts text string.
   - Close button zone: Interaction type (triggers dismiss), cardinality 0–1, fixed — top-right corner.
5. Variants: Four semantic styles (info, success, warning, error).
6. Layout flexibility: None.
7. Adaptive layout: No.
8. Interactions: Desktop — close button click dismisses. Mobile — swipe gesture dismisses, close button also available. Both — auto-dismisses after 5 seconds.
9. Platform: Both web and mobile.
10. Interaction delta: Yes. Desktop: close button is the primary dismiss affordance. Mobile: swipe-to-dismiss is the primary affordance, close button secondary.
11. States: Loading (spinner replaces icon while action is in progress).
12. Token source: Description only — mark as pending.
13. Token naming: ds- prefix (e.g., ds-color-feedback-info).
14. JSON schema: Yes. Draft 07. Inline sub-component shapes (not $ref).

Save both files to /tmp/
evals.expected_output: Toast.md with shell-only documentation — ownership clearly delegated to Icon and Button sub-components. Behavior section has separate Desktop and Mobile subsections showing the swipe delta. State machine documents the auto-dismiss timer. Schema with inline shapes for Icon and Button zones.
